name: Rye Craft Food & Drink
desc: Chef driven New American spot on the brick streets of downtown Plano with an open kitchen and a bar that takes its rye seriously. Get the crispy chicken or whatever the seasonal fish is, and let the bartender pick a cocktail for you. Go on a weeknight around 7 so you can actually sit at the bar.

reviews.text: Sat at the bar alone and left with two new drink obsessions.
Small menu but everything on it is dialed in.

name: Jorgs Cafe Vienna
desc: A genuinely weird and wonderful Austrian house in downtown Plano that has been doing schnitzel and strudel for decades. Order the wiener schnitzel with a Stiegl and finish with apple strudel. Weekend dinner gets loud and packed, so book ahead or come early.

reviews.text: Feels like a grandmother dining room in the best way.
The strudel alone is worth the drive.

name: Mango Thai Cuisine
desc: Strip mall Thai in West Plano that punches way above the parking lot it sits in. The panang curry and the crispy pad see ew are the moves, and yes you can ask for real Thai spicy. Lunch is fast and cheap, dinner is where the curries shine.

reviews.text: Actually tastes like home, not sweetened down.
Ask for Thai hot and mean it.

name: Lima Taverna
desc: Peruvian kitchen off Preston that does bright citrusy ceviche and a lomo saltado worth ordering twice. Get the ceviche mixto to start and a pisco sour while you wait. Small dining room, so a reservation saves you a wait on Friday.

reviews.text: Ceviche was so fresh it ruined every other one for me.
Lomo saltado came out sizzling and gone in ten minutes.

name: Sushi Marquee
desc: Dark, loud, neon sushi room in downtown Plano that leans more party than purist. Specialty rolls and the sashimi platters are the draw, and happy hour is where the value is. Come early evening if you want to hear your friends talk.

reviews.text: Happy hour rolls are absurdly good for the price.
Vibe is a whole night out, not just dinner.

name: Mudleaf Coffee
desc: Independent espresso bar in Preston Park pulling Cultivar beans with a proper full bar setup and quick pastries. The oat flat white is the safe order, the seasonal specials are the fun one. Great in the late afternoon when the light hits the patio.

reviews.text: Flat white was perfect temp, no burnt milk anywhere.
Small but the patio in the afternoon is underrated.

name: The Fillmore Pub
desc: Independent Irish style pub that has anchored downtown Plano since 2007, all dark wood and regulars who know the bartender. Craft cocktails are legit but the rotating local drafts are why people stay. Live music nights get shoulder to shoulder, so grab a booth early.

reviews.text: The kind of bar where you go for one and leave at close.
Bartenders remember your drink after two visits.

name: 32 Degrees Rooftop Bar
desc: Rooftop above Urban Crust with an actual ice topped bar rail and views over the downtown Plano brick streets. Get a cocktail up top, then go downstairs for a brick oven pizza if you get hungry. Sunset on a clear evening is the whole reason to go.

reviews.text: The ice rail keeps your drink cold the entire time. Genius.
Come at sunset or do not bother.

name: Russell Creek Park
desc: North Plano big open green space with shaded creek trail, disc golf, sand volleyball and fields that fill with pickup games on weekends. Bring a disc or a ball and you will find someone to play with. Evenings under the tree line are the best part.

reviews.text: Disc golf course here is way better than it has any right to be.
Perfect sunset picnic spot, tons of shade.

name: Heritage Farmstead Museum
desc: An actual 1891 Victorian farmstead sitting in the middle of Plano with goats, sheep, a windmill and the original house. Take the guided house tour, then wander the grounds and meet the animals. Cool mornings and their seasonal evening events are when it is at its best.

reviews.text: Had no idea this was hiding on 15th Street. Goats included.
Tour guide clearly loves this place. Charming as hell.

name: Haggard Park
desc: The green heart of the downtown Plano Arts District, with a pond, big shade trees and the 1908 Interurban Railway Museum sitting right on it. Grab coffee on 15th, sit by the water, then walk the antique shops and boutiques on the brick streets. Weekends bring markets, festivals and free music at nearby McCall Plaza.

reviews.text: Coffee, park, vintage shopping, all in four blocks.
The old rail museum on the corner is a genuinely cool free stop.
